correctness.rationale: For w=Rz and e=Uz−w in the open half-unit square S, v=Ue lies in the diamond D=US. Its fractional rounding residual r=v−N(v) remains in D: if a coordinate has magnitude above 1/2, it is the only such coordinate and subtracting its signed unit strictly decreases the Manhattan norm. Neither v=Qz−Uw nor any attainable rotation coordinate has half-integer ties. Writing q=N(v) gives Rw=Qz−q and U(Rw)=Qw+Ur with Ur in S, so R²w=Qw. The image is invariant, hence R⁴w=−w and R⁸w=w, ruling out all proper period divisors at nonzero w. Periodic points have predecessors, and (2,0) has none: its inverse-rotated center has Manhattan distance 2(√2−1)>1/√2 from the nearest lattice point. In the preimage diamond, all distinct lattice pairs are unit-coordinate neighbors, so three points would give a triangle, impossible. The four equal overlaps contribute half their summed areas to double coverage; the diamond's area is one, so the uncovered and doubly covered areas agree. Weyl averaging over a rectangular box is a product of two geometric averages, with at least one irrational coefficient per nonzero frequency. Polygonal boundaries are null. This proves the densities, with periodic density equal to image density.
residual_risks: The independent counts are a finite orbit/preimage check, not a density estimate used in the proof. The analytic claim depends on nearest-integer quantization and the exact 45-degree angle.
